From the tīrtha of Saptagodāvarī, the lord Bhīmeśvara
shines in the form of a liṅga, for the enjoyment and liberation of mortals here. 19.
Having beheld the lord Bhīmeśvara in front of Nakulīśa,
even terrifying sins are destroyed that very moment. 120.
From Bhūteśvara, Bhasmagātra manifested itself here of its own accord,
in the southern part of Bhīmeśa. Having worshipped it with effort, 21,
whatever fruit is attained from the proper Pāśupata yoga practiced for a hundred years,
that is obtained from the sight of Bhasmagātra. 22.
Beside Nakulīśvara is the god known as Svayambhū;
Hara revealed himself in Kāśī by his own will in the shape of a liṅga. 23.

4.69.m: A person who worships the svayambhu liṅga after bathing in the Siddhihrada,
in front of Mahālakṣmīśvara, will never again partake of rebirth. 24.
Near the Prayāga tīrtha stands a temple shining like coral,
a great temple of Vārāha named Dharaṇī. 25.
Having arrived from the Vindhya mountain, hearing that the god had come
with his retinue, seers, and gods from the caves of Mandara, 26,
that Dharaṇīvārāha must be beheld in Kāśī with devotion.
He rescues one who has taken refuge, sunk in the ocean of misfortune. 27.
Beside Karṇikāra is the leader of the gaṇas, radiant like the karṇikāra flower;
bearing a mace in hand, he removes thousands of afflictions and should be worshipped. 28.
Having worshipped the leader of the gaṇas standing in the western direction
from that Dharaṇīvārāha, one attains the station of leadership among the gaṇas. 29.
From Hemakūṭa, the liṅga Virūpākṣa appeared here;
seen to the south of Maheśvara, it delivers one from the cycle of existence. 130.
From Gaṅgādvāra came the liṅga Himastheśa, possessing a lustre like snow;
it should be beheld to the west of Brahmanāla, bestowing siddhi here. 31.
The chief of the gaṇas and other mighty gaṇas,
measuring seventy million, O lord, arrived from Mount Kailāsa. 32.
Fortresses resembling the seven heavens were erected by them here,
provided with excellent gateways, mechanical devices, and formidable door-panels, 33,
abounding with millions upon millions of warriors, accompanied by all prosperity, 34,
made of gold, silver, copper, bronze, brass, and lead,
charming with loadstones, strong, and scraping the clouds.

4.69.s: tataḥ śailaṃ mahādurgaṃ taiḥ kāśīparitaḥ kṛtam.. 35 ..
4.69.d: ततः शैलं महादुर्गं तैः काशीपरितः कृतम्.. 35 ..
4.69.m: Then a great mountain rampart was constructed by them around Kāśī. 35.
A deep moat was also dug, filled with the waters of Matsyodarī;
Matsyodarī became twofold, flowing both outside and inside. 36.
That great and famous tīrtha merged with the waters of the Gaṅgā.
Whenever the Gaṅgā's water expands here along the course of cosmic dissolution, 37,
then the Matsyodarī tīrtha is reached by virtue of religious merit.
At that time, an eclipse of the sun or moon has a hundred times ten million times the merit. 38.
All festival occasions are there alone; all tīrthas are truly there;
all liṅgas are there alone, because of the Gaṅgā and Matsyodarī. 39.

4.69.m: People who bathe anywhere in Matsyodarī,
and make offerings of funeral cakes, do not sleep in a mother's womb again. 140.
This Avimukta kṣetra assumed the shape of a fish,
and the circling water of the heavenly river is seen around it. 41.
Those men who take their bath in Matsyodarī are the best of men;
even having committed many sins, they do not see the city of the son of the Sun. 42.

4.69.m: Thus the sacred ford was made by that dweller of Kailāsa, O lord—
by the leader of the gaṇas, exceedingly great, whose deeds are exceedingly noble.
The liṅga called Bhūrbhuvaḥ, from Mount Gandhamādana,
manifested here of its own accord, to the east of that leader of the gaṇas.
Beholding the Bhūrbhuva liṅga, meritorious people dwell
for a very long time in Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and Maharloka, enjoying divine pleasures.
The great liṅga Hāṭakeśa, accompanied by the Bhogavatī,
came here of its own accord from the bottom of the seventh Pātāla, O lord.
And here its great temple, by Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and other chiefs,
was constructed with great effort out of heaps of jewels, rubies, and gems.
That golden liṅga, worshipped with garlands of gems,
is to be worshipped with effort to the east of Īśāneśvara.
Having worshipped that liṅga with devotion, a man attains all prosperity;
having enjoyed countless pleasures, he attains nirvana in the end.
From the sky, from a star, a liṅga consisting of light arrived here;
in front of the Jñānavāpī is that liṅga, Tārakeśvara.
Liberating knowledge is obtained from properly worshipping that liṅga.

4.69.d: ज्ञानवाप्यां नरः स्नात्वा तारकेशं विलोक्य च .. 54 ..
4.69.m: A man, having bathed in the Jñānavāpī and beheld Tārakeśa,
having performed the rites of twilight worship and the rest, having gratified the ancestors,
and maintaining a vow of silence, wise, until the darśana of the liṅga,
is freed from all sins and attains eternal merit;
and in the end [he obtains] the liberating knowledge, through which knowledge he is set free.
And Kirāteśa also manifested here from Kirāta,
where formerly the divine Lord assumed the form of a hunter.
Having bowed to that Kirāteśvara liṅga, [which is] after Bhārabhūteśvara,
a man never again lies in the womb of a mother.
Coming from the city of Laṅkā, the liṅga named Marukeśvara,

4.69.s: liṃgaṃ yadarcanātpuṃsāṃ na bhayaṃ rakṣasāṃ bhavet .. 59 ..
4.69.d: लिंगं यदर्चनात्पुंसां न भयं रक्षसां भवेत् .. 59 ..
4.69.m: from whose worship men have no fear of demons—
in the south-western quarter is that liṅga called Nirṛteśvara,
worshipped behind Paulastya-Rāghava, removing all wicked [beings].
The liṅga that loves holy waters, from the place of Jalaliṅga as well,
arrived and settled in the middle of the waters of the Gaṅgā.
Its most wondrous temple is seen in the midst of the Gaṅgā,
made of every metal, excellent, auspicious, made of every precious gem.
Even today it is seen by some through the weight of their heap of merit.
The excellent liṅga arrived here from the Koṭīśvara sacred ford too;
from beholding that liṅga at the time of a crore of liṅgas, merit [is gained];
[it is] the best, west of Jyeṣṭheśvara, bestowing supreme perfection.
Arising from the submarine fire's mouth, the liṅga Analeśvara here,
worshipped in front of Naleśvara, bestows all perfections.
Coming from the Virajas sacred ford, the god of gods, the three-eyed one,
took his abode in heaven within a liṅga perfected from beginninglessness.
At the holy Pilipilā sacred ford, which bestows liberation upon all,
Oṃkāra revealed himself of his own accord from Amarakaṇṭaka.

4.69.s: tadādyaṃ tārakakṣetraṃ yadā gaṃgā na cāgatā ..

4.69.m: That was the primeval liberating field when the Gaṅgā had not yet arrived,
when Kāśī manifested indeed for the uplift of the three worlds.
Then the great liṅga of that form manifested of its own accord;
none other than the Lord comprehends its majesty.
These great abodes, O Lord, he brought together,
leaving only a single portion behind in each of their respective fields.
The sacred ones have arrived here with their entire essence, not otherwise.
And their charming temples all around scratch the clouds, O Lord,
composed of many metals, wondrous, brilliant with all gems,
from the mere darśana of whose pinnacle liberation is obtained.
Even upon merely hearing the name of these liṅgas, O best of the gods,
the heaps of sins arising from a thousand births are destroyed.
Now what command here is to be carried out by me, O Lord?

4.69.s: prasādī kriyatāṃso pi siddho maṃtavya eva hi .. 74 ..
4.69.d: प्रसादी क्रियतांसो पि सिद्धो मंतव्य एव हि .. 74 ..
4.69.m: Let it be graciously bestowed; it should surely be considered already accomplished.
Skanda said:
Hearing these words of Nandin, Hara, the lord of the god of gods,
propitiated the son of Śilāda with faith and spoke thus, O pitcher-born one:
The holy god of gods said:
"Well done by you, O Nandin, bestower of eternal bliss!
Carry out my instruction now, and deploy the Caṇḍīs.
Indeed, wherever the nine crores of Cāmuṇḍās dwell,
accompanied by their deities, spirits, vetālas, and Bhairavas,
station them all around in every fortress, in the form of Durgā,
with their mounts, forces, and weapons, for the protection of the city."
Skanda said:
Having thus instructed Nandin, Mṛḍa, accompanied by Mṛḍānī,
went to the Traiviṣṭapa sacred field, the sprouting-ground for the seed of liberation.
The son of Śilāda, placing the command of Īśa upon his head,
summoned the Durgās from everywhere and stationed them in each fortress.
Hearing this chapter, pregnant with holy shrines,
a man attains both heaven and final liberation in succession through faith.
Having heard this [account of] the sixty-eight great sacred places,

4.69.d: न जातु प्रविशेन्मर्त्यो जनन्या जाठरीं दरीम् .. 182 .. ..
4.69.m: a mortal shall never enter the cave of a mother's womb.

4.69.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंडे उत्तरार्धेऽष्टषष्ट्यायतनसमागमो नामैकोनसप्ततितमोध्यायः .. 69 .. ..
4.69.m: Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, named 'The Gathering of the Sixty-Eight Shrines', in the second half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa, in the fourth [part of] the holy Skandapurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

4.70.m: Agastya said:
O son of Kātyāyanī, tell how the goddesses were deployed
by Nandin, who delights the universe, by command of the god of gods.

4.70.m: Which deities were stationed where for the protection of Avimukta?

4.70.m: Be gracious to me, O god, and tell them to me in truth.
Hearing this speech spoken by Agastya, the son born of Mahādeva's body
joyfully related who was stationed where in the Ānandavana.
Skanda said:
In Vārāṇasī is Viśālākṣī, who grants the supreme desire of the sacred field;
she remains positioned behind, having made the Viśālatīrtha at the Gaṅgā.

4.70.m: Bathing in the Viśālatīrtha and bowing down to Viśālākṣī,

4.70.s: viśālāṃ labhate lakṣmīṃ paratreha ca śarmadām .. 5 ..
4.70.d: विशालां लभते लक्ष्मीं परत्रेह च शर्मदाम् .. 5 ..
4.70.m: one obtains vast fortune, bestowing happiness both here and in the hereafter.
On the third day of the dark fortnight of the month of Bhādra, by men intent on fasting,
having kept vigil through the night in the vicinity of Viśālākṣī,
fourteen young girls should be carefully fed in the morning,
adorned according to one's ability with garlands, garments, and ornaments.
Then, having broken the fast together with sons and servants,
one completely attains the fruit of dwelling in Vārāṇasī, O pitcher-born one.
On that lunar day, a great pilgrimage is to be made by residents of the sacred field,
for the pacification of afflictions and for obtaining the lotus-like nirvāṇa.
In Vārāṇasī, Viśālākṣī is to be worshipped diligently
with incenses, lamps, auspicious garlands, and charming offerings,
with ornaments of gems, pearls, and the like, with variegated canopies and fly-whisks,
and with auspicious, unused silks perfumed with fragrant scents.
By residents anywhere, for the sake of the prosperity of liberation's fortune,
even the smallest gift given to Viśālākṣī by the best of men
leads to infinity in both worlds, O sage.

4.70.s: viśālākṣī mahāpīṭhe dattaṃ japtaṃ hutaṃ stutam .. 13 ..
4.70.d: विशालाक्षी महापीठे दत्तं जप्तं हुतं स्तुतम् .. 13 ..
4.70.m: Whatever is given, muttered, offered into fire, or praised at the great seat of Viśālākṣī
has liberation as its final fruit; no doubt should be entertained here.
From worshipping Viśālākṣī, a husband endowed with wealth and beauty,
adorned with virtues, good conduct, and the like, is obtained by maiden girls here;
a good son is obtained by pregnant women, conception is obtained by barren women,
and great good fortune is obtained by women bereft of fortune.
Widowhood is never experienced by widows in any future birth.
By women or men who desire the supreme nirvāṇa,
Viśālākṣī, the granter of desires, should be heard of, seen, and worshipped in Kāśī.
Beyond that is another, the Lalitātīrtha, in the vicinity of Gaṅgākeśava;
there resides goddess Lalitā, the supreme protectress of the sacred field.
She should be worshipped diligently for the increase of all prosperity;

4.70.s: lalitāpūjakānāṃ ca jātu vighno na jāyate .. 19 ..

4.70.m: and for worshippers of Lalitā, no obstacle ever arises.
Having worshipped Lalitā on the second day of the dark fortnight of Āśvina,

4.70.m: O sage, the goddess Gaurī Viśvabhujā stands in front of Viśālākṣī,

4.70.m: During the autumn Navarātra, a pilgrimage should be diligently undertaken
to the goddess Viśvabhujā, for the fulfillment of all desires.

4.70.m: A person who does not bow to the goddess Viśvabhujā in Vārāṇasī—

4.70.s: tāṃ praṇamya naro bhaktyā vipadabdhau na majjati .. 26 ..
4.70.d: तां प्रणम्य नरो भक्त्या विपदब्धौ न मज्जति .. 26 ..

Likewise Aindrī, holding the thunderbolt in her hand, seated on an elephant chariot,

Near Skandeśvara is Kaumārī, mounted on a peacock vehicle;
she should be beheld with effort for the attainment of great fruits.
To the south of Maheśvara, the goddess Māheśvarī,
having a bull for her mount, should be worshipped by men; she grants abundant cattle and great virtue.
Near Nirvāṇanarasiṃha, by those desiring liberation,
Nārasiṃhī should be worshipped, with her charming arm bearing the uplifted discus.
Brāhmī, riding on a swan, stands to the west of Brahmeśa,
beneficent, splashing sips of water poured from her water-pot.
For the awakening of knowledge of Brahman, she should be worshipped day by day in Kāśī
by brahmins and ascetics who constantly comprehend their true essence.
Scattering obstacles in every direction with great arrows shot from the Śārṅga bow,
one should take refuge in Nārāyaṇī in Kāśī.
To the west of Gopīgovinda, her raised forefinger threatening, a whirling discus in hand,

Then, having worshipped Gaurī situated to the north of Virūpākṣa and Devayānī

4.70.s: pūjayitvā naro bhaktyā vāṃchitāṃ labhate śriyam .. 36 ..
4.70.d: पूजयित्वा नरो भक्त्या वांछितां लभते श्रियम् .. 36 ..
4.70.m: with devotion, a person obtains desired prosperity.
Śaileśvarī, residing near Śaileśvara, is to be worshipped,
threatening with her forefinger any contact arising from distress.
After bathing in Citrakūpa, which grants wonderful rewards to mortals,
beholding Citragupteśvara, and worshipping Citraghaṇṭā,
even if full of many sins or having abandoned the path of righteousness,
a person who worships Citraghaṇṭā will not be inscribed in Citragupta's ledger.

4.70.s: yoṣidvā puruṣo vāpi citraghaṃṭāṃ na yorcayet ..
4.70.d: योषिद्वा पुरुषो वापि चित्रघंटां न योर्चयेत् ..
4.70.m: Whatever woman or man does not worship Citraghaṇṭā,
thousands of obstacles attend them at every step in Kāśī.
On the third day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, a pilgrimage should be undertaken with care;

And having worshipped Citraghaṇṭā with items of grand worship,
one never hears the bell around the neck of Death's buffalo in this world.
Having bowed to Citragrīvā to the east of Citrāṅgadeśvara,
a living creature will never behold the terrifying torments of Yama.

Nigaḍabhañjanī, a person is never bound by fetters.

having eaten only one meal, out of devotion, desiring release from bonds.

4.70.m: For even a kinsman who is far away will quickly return

4.70.s: baṃdī padajuṣāṃ puṃsāṃ śraddhayā nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 4.2.70.50 ..
4.70.m: to men who worship the feet of Bandī with faith; of this there is no doubt.
If she is attended upon by observing some discipline,
Kāśī, dispeller of doubts, quickly fulfills all desires.
The goddess, holding a heavy chisel in her hand, shatters the bonds of devotees;

The goddess behind Paśupati, in the presence of Amṛteśvara,
must be bowed down to with effort, after bathing in the Amṛta well.

4.72.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ caturthe kāśīkhaṃḍa uttarārdhe durgāvijayo nāma dvisaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 72 ..
4.72.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां चतुर्थे काशीखंड उत्तरार्धे दुर्गाविजयो नाम द्विसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः .. 72 ..
4.72.m: Thus ends the seventy-second chapter, named 'The Victory over Durgā', in the latter half of the Kāśīkhaṇḍa in the glorious Skandapurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.
